     6	[gobreaker][repo-url] implements the [Circuit Breaker pattern](https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/dn589784.aspx) in Go.
     7	
     8	Installation
     9	------------
    10	
    11	```
    12	go get github.com/sony/gobreaker
    13	```
    14	
    15	Usage
    16	-----
    17	
    18	The struct `CircuitBreaker` is a state machine to prevent sending requests that are likely to fail.
    19	The function `NewCircuitBreaker` creates a new `CircuitBreaker`.
    20	
    21	```go
    22	func NewCircuitBreaker(st Settings) *CircuitBreaker
    23	```
    24	
    25	You can configure `CircuitBreaker` by the struct `Settings`:
    26	
    27	```go
    28	type Settings struct {
    29		Name          string
    30		MaxRequests   uint32
    31		Interval      time.Duration
    32		Timeout       time.Duration
    33		ReadyToTrip   func(counts Counts) bool
    34		OnStateChange func(name string, from State, to State)
    35		IsSuccessful  func(err error) bool
    36	}
    37	```
    38	
    39	- `Name` is the name of the `CircuitBreaker`.
    40	
    41	- `MaxRequests` is the maximum number of requests allowed to pass through
    42	  when the `CircuitBreaker` is half-open.
    43	  If `MaxRequests` is 0, `CircuitBreaker` allows only 1 request.
    44	
    45	- `Interval` is the cyclic period of the closed state
    46	  for `CircuitBreaker` to clear the internal `Counts`, described later in this section.
    47	  If `Interval` is 0, `CircuitBreaker` doesn't clear the internal `Counts` during the closed state.
    48	
    49	- `Timeout` is the period of the open state,
    50	  after which the state of `CircuitBreaker` becomes half-open.
    51	  If `Timeout` is 0, the timeout value of `CircuitBreaker` is set to 60 seconds.
    52	
    53	- `ReadyToTrip` is called with a copy of `Counts` whenever a request fails in the closed state.
    54	  If `ReadyToTrip` returns true, `CircuitBreaker` will be placed into the open state.
    55	  If `ReadyToTrip` is `nil`, default `ReadyToTrip` is used.
    56	  Default `ReadyToTrip` returns true when the number of consecutive failures is more than 5.
    57	
    58	- `OnStateChange` is called whenever the state of `CircuitBreaker` changes.
    59	
    60	- `IsSuccessful` is called with the error returned from a request.
    61	  If `IsSuccessful` returns true, the error is counted as a success.
    62	  Otherwise the error is counted as a failure.
    63	  If `IsSuccessful` is nil, default `IsSuccessful` is used, which returns false for all non-nil errors.
    64	
    65	The struct `Counts` holds the numbers of requests and their successes/failures:
    66	
    67	```go
    68	type Counts struct {
    69		Requests             uint32
    70		TotalSuccesses       uint32
    71		TotalFailures        uint32
    72		ConsecutiveSuccesses uint32
    73		ConsecutiveFailures  uint32
    74	}
    75	```
    76	
    77	`CircuitBreaker` clears the internal `Counts` either
    78	on the change of the state or at the closed-state intervals.
    79	`Counts` ignores the results of the requests sent before clearing.
    80	
    81	`CircuitBreaker` can wrap any function to send a request:
    82	
    83	```go
    84	func (cb *CircuitBreaker) Execute(req func() (interface{}, error)) (interface{}, error)
    85	```

    87	The method `Execute` runs the given request if `CircuitBreaker` accepts it.
    88	`Execute` returns an error instantly if `CircuitBreaker` rejects the request.

    99	func Get(url string) ([]byte, error) {

   110			}
   111	
   112			return body, nil
   113		})

   116		}
   117

   119	}

{"exit_code": 0, "stdout": "# How StateRadar works: instructions for an LLM

You are an agent in a repository that uses StateRadar. This document tells you what the system is. It shows how information flows through the system. It lists the rules that bind you. The language layer (STE/DTK) is a separate concern.

## 1. What this is

The pack treats a Harel-style statechart as the specification and the test oracle for one stateful component. The division of work does not change. You extract, classify, draft, and propose. Deterministic code verifies your outputs. The human owner decides domain semantics.

Never fill a specification gap with your own judgment, however plausible. Your value is completeness and honesty, not decisiveness.

## 2. The objects

* **Machine boundary**: the scope statement declares one bounded component. The machine boundary is this component, not the whole system.
* **State**: a state is a mode of the component. Implicit states count. Enumerate the reachable combinations of boolean flags and nullable references. These combinations are the real state space.
* **Event**: an event has one of three sources: external (boundary calls), internal (timers, delivered results), or an undesired variant (`UV-nn`). Derive the undesired variants per source from a fixed checklist (generated from `formats/rules.toml`):

<!-- generated:rules key=uv-categories -->
* loss or failure of the source (F-12, sidecar key: `loss`)
* delay beyond timeout (F-13, sidecar key: `delay`)
* duplication (F-14, sidecar key: `duplication`)
* out-of-order or stale arrival, especially after cancellation or shutdown (F-15, sidecar key: `out-of-order`)
* contradictory simultaneous inputs (F-16, sidecar key: `contradiction`)
* spontaneous commission — an event with no legitimate trigger (spurious wakeup, callback without a matching request, unsolicited push) (F-17, sidecar key: `commission`)
* subtle value fault — a plausible but wrong payload (foreign session or entity id, stale epoch or generation counter) (F-18, sidecar key: `value`)
<!-- /generated:rules -->

  The coverage table must show every category. Write a reason for each `n/a`.
* **Interaction pairs** (`P-nna/b`): an interaction pair is a cross-source event pair on one shared entity, in both orderings. Per-source checklists structurally miss races between sources. Interaction pairs close this gap.
* **Disposition**: each matrix cell has exactly one disposition: `transition → <target>`, `handle`, `ignore (documented)`, `ignore (accidental)`, `defer (queued)`, `reject`, or `UNSPECIFIED`. The values `ignore (accidental)` and `UNSPECIFIED` are holes.
* **Guards**: formalizable guard groups get z3 proofs: pairwise disjointness, coverage, and boundary probes. Each group ends as `proven`, `violation`, or `not-formalizable: <reason>`. Never skip a guard group silently.
* **Invariants**: `NAT` marks an assumption about the environment. Cite the assumption into the callee or upstream. `SYS` marks an obligation of the system. Check each SYS invariant state by state.
* **Doctrine lines** (`DOC-n`): extract every normative sentence from the requirements. Map each doctrine line to an invariant, a disposition constraint, or an explicit rejection. An unmapped doctrine line is an error.
* **Provenance**: every behavioural claim carries one label: `explicit-requirement`, `observed-in-code`, `observed-in-tests`, `inferred`, or `proposed`. Code and test citations carry a fragment: `file:line ("fragment")`. The checkers verify the fragment near that line.
* **Questions** (`Q-nn`): every hole, contradiction, and violated assumption becomes a question. Only the human can answer it. Drop nothing in consolidation. Every hole cell carries `→ Q-nn`.
* **Decision records** (`DR-nnn.yaml`): a decision record holds the human's answers with attributed rationale. The decision records are the permanent memory. A to-be deviation without a DR is an error.
* **Sidecar and manifest**: `analysis.json` holds your machine-readable claims. `manifest.json` holds `analyzedSha` and the watch paths. The pack checker consumes both files. Git diffs against the SHA turn staleness into a CI signal.

## 3. The loop

```text
01 Scout      rank stateful components; evidence-based, read-only
02 Pilot      Part A: extract → as-is model → catalogue → matrix → guards
              → invariants → adversarial traces → open questions
              Part B: a BLIND session predicts dispositions from the
              catalogue + requirements only; a diff classifies every row
   (human)    answers the questions — interview mode: one per round,
              recommended option first (Enter default), attributed
              rationale, write-through per answer, defer stays OPEN
03 Resolution DRs, to-be model, matrix update, re-run all checkers
04 Testgen    one test per matrix cell + scenario tests from decided
              traces; red tests against current code = deviation report
              = the implementation worklist, never a test defect
   (impl.)    fix code DR by DR; docs-only DRs first (no red test
              reminds you); tests are read-only
06 Reconcile  after green: promote to-be → as-is, refresh citations at
              HEAD, write sidecar + manifest, archive superseded files
07 Test audit off-cycle: weak tests first (structure over function),
              then redundancy, deviations, gaps; propose, never delete
```

Run 06 first when the manifest reports staleness. Run 01 or 02 for a new component. For a behaviour change request, follow the standing instruction: model and DR first, code second.
## 4. Rules that do not bend

<!-- rule:R-NO-SILENT-DECISIONS -->
1. **Never decide domain semantics.** If behaviour is unclear, contradictory, or unspecified, write a question. Treat a "benign" gap as a proposal inside the question. It is never a reason to omit the question.
<!-- rule:R-REQUIREMENT-SCOPE-a -->
2. **Requirement-scope rule.** A citation covers only the scenario that its text describes. A control-trace verdict that cites a requirement must carry the line: *cited text contemplates this ordering: yes/no*. A "no" voids the verdict. Then raise a question.
<!-- rule:R-SEAM-CONTRACT -->
3. **Read callee contracts. Do not infer them.** Missing error handling at a call site is not evidence that failures propagate. Read the contract of the seam. Cite into the callee.
<!-- rule:R-EXECUTED-CHECKS -->
4. **Run checks as executed code.** You emit data. The pack verifies it with `tools/dsc_check.py` on the sidecar. When you write per-run checkers, run them and paste the output. A red checker means: fix the artefact, or fix the checker openly and re-run. Never "fix" the data to silence a check.
<!-- rule:R-PROPOSALS -->
5. **Proposals are not decisions.** Recommendations have flipped between runs on the same code. Present them, label them `proposed`, and hold them loosely. Pre-selection in the interview is presentation, not authority.
<!-- rule:R-ANTI-MIRRORING -->
6. **Tests bind to behaviour, not structure.** Assert only through the declared seam: projected state, emitted effects, and SYS invariants. Never weaken, skip, or delete a test to make it pass. A failing cell test is a finding.
<!-- rule:R-PART-B -->
7. **Part B stays blind.** The blind session gets the catalogue, the requirements, and the event contracts. It never gets the code, the matrix, or prior analyses. Do no git archaeology on deleted analyses.
<!-- rule:R-DEFERRED-OPEN -->
8. **Deferred stays OPEN.** A deferred question blocks only its own cells.
<!-- rule:R-READ-PROMPTS -->
9. **Read prompts in full.** When a task says "run prompt X" or references a prompt file (e.g. `prompts/02-pilot.md`), read the complete file before producing output. Do not guess its content from the filename, derive it from memory, or skip steps that the prompt requires. A subagent that produces the wrong number of events because it did not read the undesired-variant checklist has not executed the prompt.

## 5. What the checkers catch

The checkers catch the following defects. Do not fight them. (Generated from `formats/rules.toml` — the registry maps each line to its rule, checker, and selftest.)

<!-- generated:rules key=checker-catalogue -->
* grid totality
* disposition vocabulary
* hole → Q back-references
* DR links on ignore, reject, and defer
* behavioural-DR reverse coverage: every decided change connects to a cell
* pair → trace coverage
* guard outcomes present
* coverage-table totality
* Mermaid ↔ matrix sync
* fragment citations within ±3 lines
* manifest staleness
* blind-table row coverage
* schema validity of the sidecar
* existence of every cited DR file
* reachable states and terminal-state marking
* state names follow PA-17 (PascalCase segments or ALL-CAPS API enums)
* doctrine-line mapping totality (DOC-n → cell / invariant / rejected)
* event classification present per catalogue event (PA-4)
* abstraction statement in the matrix (PA-10)
* scope lines on citing control traces
* gate-type annotation presence on events
* opt-in cell rationale completeness and source-backed scope
* upstream-guard annotation presence on events
<!-- /generated:rules -->

## 6. Failure modes seen in real runs

Avoid these failure modes from real runs.

* Call-site inference declared a publisher failure path. The callee's contract excludes this path.
* An agent applied a recorded decision for steady state to a race. The decision never contemplated this race.
* A checklist category silently produced no variant.
* A catalogue stated gates but not remembrance semantics. Remembrance semantics say what ended entities leave behind. Blind readers misread five rows for that one omission.
* Consolidation lost findings between runs.
* An agent almost softened an expected-red test instead of reporting it.

When your Part-B diff exposes a recurring divergence class, fold it back into the pilot prompt's changelog as a rule. Single findings stay findings. The goal is not zero divergence. A blind pass that cannot disagree is dead weight.

- **Completion-report drift.** Session reports have described work
  absent from the repository: tasks marked done that were never
  committed, tags reported "pushed" that never left the workspace.
  Countermeasures that worked: acceptance criteria as executable
  commands, remote verification, paste obligations.
- **Hollow checks.** A verification mechanism was built so it could
  not fail (file-existence instead of anchor verification; anchors
  resolving into generated blocks). The countermeasure is R-RED-PROBE:
  a mechanism's failure path is demonstrated at build time.
- **Vacuous green.** A relocated test runner reported "0/0 cases
  pass" with exit 0. Discovery that finds nothing now hard-fails.
- **First-contact failures.** Across one extended session, every tool
  change shipped without a simultaneous gate arrived defective but
  green; every change built together with its red case held on first
  contact. The gate is not overhead — it is the difference.

## 7. Working on this pack

The rules above govern the analysis. These govern changes to the pack
itself — every one of them exists because its violation was observed
in real pack-development sessions.

<!-- rule:R-VERIFIED-COMPLETION -->
1. **Completion = diff + executed acceptance.** Describe only work
   that is in the committed diff, and only acceptance commands you
   ran. Paste their output under `Evidence:` in the commit body.
<!-- rule:R-RED-PROBE -->
2. **No mechanism without an observed failure.** Build the red probe
   first, watch it fail for the intended reason, then build the
   mechanism, then watch the probe pass. Paste both runs. A check
   that has never been red proves nothing (see §5's CI note).
<!-- rule:R-REMOTE-TRUTH -->
3. **"Pushed" means the remote says so.** Verify tags and pushes with
   `git ls-remote` and paste it. Your working copy is not the release.
<!-- rule:R-GREEN-MAIN -->
4. **Green before push.** Run the full gate set (§5) before every

plan](plan-model-cascade.md); broader project work is in the
[roadmap](roadmap.md).

This optional workflow sends supplied text to DeepSeek and TypeSafe. Set
`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` and `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in the environment. Each pilot uses
a separate SQLite ledger stored outside the repository. The default ledger
limit is $2, expressed as 2,000,000 microdollars.

```bash
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/state/stateradar"
ledger="$HOME/.local/state/stateradar/example-pilot.sqlite"
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger "$ledger" status
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger "$ledger" flash /path/to/task-and-source.txt
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger "$ledger" jev /path/to/source.txt \
  'Does the source explicitly describe the specified event ordering?' --model jev-1.14.0
```

A new ledger takes its limit from `--limit-microdollars` on the first call
(default 2,000,000). The flag only sets the initial limit: passing a different
value to an existing ledger fails, so change it with `set-limit`.

The Flash input must include the task and the source excerpts needed to do it.
Each invocation is a fresh text-only call. Flash cannot browse the repo or
execute tools through this interface. A calling agent prepares inputs, checks
citations and results, runs the deterministic checkers, and carries forward
every uncertainty and question. Jev returns a probability; it does not
establish a domain decision.

### Batch semantic checks

Use `jev-batch` to evaluate independent claims and event orderings against the
same source file in one request. Supply a JSON array such as:

```json
[
  {"id": "C1", "kind": "claim", "statement": "The component stays failed.", "line": 12, "fragment": "remains in FAILED"},
  {"id": "O1", "kind": "ordering", "statement": "A disconnect occurs after failure.", "line": 12, "fragment": "remains in FAILED"}
]
```

```bash
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger "$ledger" jev-batch \
  /path/to/source.md /path/to/checks.json --model jev-1.14.0 --output /path/to/batch.json
```

For shorter tool results, add `--summary` with `--output`. Stdout carries
the artifact path, usage, and counts by choice. The output file keeps every
judgment and its citation. For `flash`, use `--output draft.json` to save
the draft and print usage. If Flash truncates the draft, the command exits
with an error and keeps it at `draft.json.partial.json`.

Each `line` is a one-based integer line in the source file. Each `fragment` is
a single line of at least four non-space characters that occurs on a line
within three lines of it, the pack-wide citation window. The `draft-verify`
prompt asks Flash for the cited line itself; the check accepts the window.
Missing fragments, invalid lines, duplicate IDs and incomplete responses fail.
All questions see the same source and are evaluated independently. Prepare a
separate batch for another source. The response includes the source path and
content hash, citation, statement, model version, choice probabilities, token
usage, and cost. Every result is marked for review. Ordering checks also
receive an independently evaluated `ordering_scope_probability` for whether
the fragment establishes every material condition, actor, event, order and
outcome in the asserted sequence. Paraphrases count when they preserve the
meaning. Surrounding text cannot supply missing evidence. The Choice and
Noul answers may disagree; preserve both and examine the source. Confidence
and repeatability do not establish correctness. Follow the requirement-scope rule and raise a
question when its conditions require one. An API error after reservation keeps
the reservation until reconciled. Omit `--model` to use `jev-latest`; pin a
specific available version for comparable measurements.

### Draft and verify

`draft-verify` chains the two models for one source file. Flash receives the
task and the numbered source and must answer with JSON: a `claims` list (`id`,
`kind` = `claim` or `ordering`, `statement`, `line`, `fragment`) and a
`questions` list. Code rejects a draft that is not this structure, and a draft
cut off at the output budget (`finish_reason=length`); either way the raw text
is saved next to the output with the extension replaced (`--output
review.json` gives `review.draft.txt`) and is not printed. The default output
budget is 12000 tokens: 4096 truncated a 248-line source, whose complete draft
then took about 5,200, so 12000 leaves headroom (the ledger reserves 1.2 times
the budget for output). Each claim's citation is then checked against the
source with the same rule as `jev-batch`. Claims that fail keep their reason
in `citation_check` and are never sent to Jev. The citable claims go to Jev in
one batch.

```bash
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger "$ledger" draft-verify \
  docs/requirements.md /path/to/task.md --output /path/to/draft-review.json \
  --model jev-1.14.0
```

The result records the source path and hash, the Flash and Jev usage, every
claim with its citation check and Jev judgment, and every draft question. The
command prints a summary (counts, citation failures, Jev choices, usage); the
full result is only in the output file. If Jev fails after the draft was paid
for, the result is still written, with the error in `verification.error` and
no Jev judgments, and the command exits 1. Everything is marked for review;
nothing is accepted. `prompts/02-pilot.md` ("Model routing") says which pilot
steps use this command and how the calling agent consolidates the result,
including the rule that an ordering counts as source-backed only when Jev's
choice is `supported` and its scope probability is at least 0.5. That cut-off
is provisional and uncalibrated: it can only turn an ordering into a question
and never accepts one. The command needs both API keys. Every command that
takes `--output` checks before any request that the output is not a directory
and its directory is writable.

### Draft matrix cells

`draft-cells` drafts disposition-matrix cells (the 02-pilot routing variant
`flash-writes`, roadmap entry 11 item 2). The task file is JSON written by the
steering agent: `states` (each a `name` and the `condition` that defines it),
`events` (each an `id` and a `gist`) and optional `notes`; names and ids are
one word, and rule 10 of the routing section (finding-neutral tasks) applies
to all of it. Flash must answer with one cell per state and event (`state`,
`event`, `disposition`, `target` for a transition, `line`, `fragment`, `note`)
plus `questions`. Code checks each cell: known state and event, the closed
disposition vocabulary of `formats/rules.toml`, a transition target among the
states, no target on other dispositions, the citation rule of `jev-batch`, and
one cell per pair; it lists the pairs without a cell. Every matrix tool splits
table rows on `|`, so a fragment with a `|` is cut to its longest verbatim
piece without one (refused if that piece is too short) and a note's `|`
becomes `/`. Every clean cell goes to one Jev batch as a claim that names the
state with its condition, the event with its gist and the drafted outcome. The
default output budget is 16384 tokens, the Flash maximum; split the events
across task files when a draft is cut off.

The result JSON holds every cell with its problems and Jev judgment, the
missing pairs, the draft questions and the usage. The command also writes a
matrix block next to the JSON (`cells.json` gives `cells.md`): the 02-pilot
cell form in sub-tables of eight events, then a review list (cells with
problems, cells Jev did not judge `supported`, missing pairs) and the draft
questions. A hole or a cell with a problem carries `→ Q-?` (a cell with a
problem also loses its citation), and a missing cell reads `MISSING`, so
`dsc_check.py` fails until the agent has decided each. Nothing is accepted:
the agent checks every cell against the source. A draft that is not the
required JSON, or is cut off, is kept as `cells.draft.txt`. The command needs
both API keys.

`python3 tools/draft_cells.py compare cells.json … --sidecar analysis.json`
needs no key: it compares the drafts with the run's final sidecar and counts
each drafted cell as unchanged, changed (disposition, target or citation) or
dropped, split by Jev's choice, and lists the final cells no draft held.
Add `--output compare.json` to keep all rows in the report file and print
aggregate counts.

```bash
python3 tools/local_models.py --ledger "$ledger" draft-cells \
  pool/channel.go /path/to/cells-task.json --output /path/to/cells.json \
  --model jev-1.14.0
```

### Evaluate a batch against reviewed examples

`tools/jev_eval.py` compares one saved `jev-batch` result (its `--output` file
or redirected stdout) with independently reviewed labels. It does not read
`draft-verify` output, which nests the judgments under `claims`. It runs
locally and makes no provider calls. The labels use the same source hash and
check identity as the batch, plus an attributed reviewer and the expected
verdict. For example, if the saved batch was produced from the exact source
and check shown below, a label file has this shape (replace the example hash
with the batch's actual `source_sha256`):

```json

  "source_sha256": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa",
  "checks": {
    "C1": {

      "source": "/path/to/source.md", "line": 12,
      "fragment": "remains in FAILED", "expected": "supported",
      "reviewer": "attributed independent reviewer"
    }
  }
}
```

```bash
python3 tools/jev_eval.py /path/to/labels.json /path/to/batch.json
```

checks attribution is present, but cannot establish reviewer independence or
whether a label is correct. It requires identical case IDs, source hashes and
check identities and refuses empty or mismatched datasets. It reports the
confusion matrix, exact matches, IDs judged supported against a non-supported
label, unclear IDs, and the batch's reported input tokens and estimated cost.
It does not evaluate the separate ordering-scope probability, choose a
threshold, or include the costs of any other calls. Review all judgments and
keep any unresolved domain question open. See [the cascade
plan](plan-model-cascade.md) for dataset and end-to-end evaluation
requirements.

repeat both batched and individual calls with the same source and questions.

input tokens. Repeated evaluations can include a changing, irrelevant nonce in

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import sys
from typing import Any

from gen_analysis_sidecar import _parse_cell
from local_models import _citation_error


WINDOW_PROMPT = """Propose source-grounded concurrency schedules for this component.
Use only the supplied source. Domain intent stays open. Return a JSON object
with one key candidates, a list of up to 8 concise schedule objects. Each object has
observation, mutator, branch, caller_outcomes, inventory, pending, later_effect
(nonempty strings), and steps (2 to 10 ordered objects, each with actor,
action, integer line and verbatim fragment from that numbered source line).
Keep every string under 180 characters. Use at most 7 steps per candidate.
Each fragment is a short verbatim substring of one line; use no line ranges.

Enumerate observes, locks, commits, waits and returns within each operation.
An observation includes failed nonblocking receive/send, readiness and empty
queues, not just assignments or explicit boolean expressions. Distinguish a
pointer being present from the readiness or contents of the object it names.
For each observation before a lock or commit, choose specific other operations
that can change it in the gap. Cross each changed observation with each
feasible branch after the gap. For capacity guards check equality and room
below separately. State whether the earlier observation is repeated. Show
which caller now returns or waits, what is buffered and what is pending.
Follow a third caller or later matching input where this distinguishes
outcomes. Include generation changes, repeated completions, and callbacks
that may hold or reacquire a lock where applicable. Separate impossible
orders, or omit them with no claim. Prefer concrete changed outcomes over
ordinary serial calls. Do not prescribe fixes or claim tests ran.
"""


def review_windows(text: str, source: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Retain candidates with deterministic problems marked for review."""
    fence = re.fullmatch(r'\s*```(?:json)?\s*(.*?)\s*```\s*', text, re.S)
    raw = json.loads(fence[1] if fence else text)
    candidates = raw.get('candidates') if isinstance(raw, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(candidates, list) or not 1 <= len(candidates) <= 12:
        raise ValueError('expected 1 to 12 candidates')
    result = []
    fields = ('observation', 'mutator', 'branch', 'caller_outcomes', 'inventory', 'pending', 'later_effect')
    lines = source.splitlines()
    for number, item in enumerate(candidates, 1):
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            raise ValueError(f'candidate {number} must be an object')
        problems = [f'missing or empty {name}' for name in fields
                    if not isinstance(item.get(name), str) or not item[name].strip()]
        steps = item.get('steps')
        if not isinstance(steps, list) or not 2 <= len(steps) <= 10:
            problems.append('expected 2 to 10 ordered steps')
        else:
            for idx, step in enumerate(steps, 1):
                if not isinstance(step, dict) or not all(
                        isinstance(step.get(key), str) and step[key].strip()
                        for key in ('actor', 'action')):
                    problems.append(f'step {idx}: actor and action required')
                    continue
                error = _citation_error(lines, step.get('line'), step.get('fragment'))
                if error:
                    problems.append(f'step {idx}: {error}')
        result.append({**item, 'id': f'W-{number:02}', 'problems': problems, 'review_required': True})
    return result


def identifiers(data: dict, field: str, pattern: str, *, optional: bool = False) -> list[str]:
    values = data.get(field, [] if optional else None)
    if (not isinstance(values, list) or (not values and not optional)
            or not all(isinstance(value, str) and re.fullmatch(pattern, value) for value in values)
            or len(set(values)) != len(values)):
        raise ValueError(f'{field} must contain distinct valid identifiers')
    return values


def render_matrix(data: object, repo: Path) -> str:
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise ValueError('expected a matrix object')
    states = identifiers(data, 'states', r'[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_.]*')
    events = identifiers(data, 'events', r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*')
    terminal = identifiers(data, 'terminal', r'[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_.]*', optional=True)
    if not set(terminal) <= set(states):
        raise ValueError('terminal names must be declared states')
    abstraction = data.get('abstraction')
    if not isinstance(abstraction, str) or not abstraction.strip() or '\n' in abstraction:
        raise ValueError('abstraction must be a nonempty single line')
    cells = data.get('cells')
    if not isinstance(cells, list):
        raise ValueError('cells must be an array')
    grid = {}
    sources: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    repo = repo.resolve()
    errors = []
    for cell in cells:
        if not isinstance(cell, dict):
            raise ValueError('each cell must be an object')
        state, event = cell.get('state'), cell.get('event')
        if state not in states or event not in events:
            errors.append(f'{state} x {event}: unknown state or event')
            continue
        pair = state, event
        if pair in grid:
            errors.append(f'{state} x {event}: duplicate cell')
            continue
        try:
            grid[pair] = render_cell(cell, states, repo, sources)
        except ValueError as error:
            errors.append(f'{state} x {event}: {error}')
    missing = [(state, event) for state in states for event in events if (state, event) not in grid]
    if missing and not errors:
        errors.append(f'{len(missing)} missing cells: ' + ', '.join(f'{s} x {e}' for s, e in missing[:12]))
    if errors:
        raise ValueError('\n'.join(errors))
    output = ['# Disposition matrix', '', f'Abstraction: {abstraction}', '',
              f'<!-- states: {", ".join(states)} -->', '']
    if terminal:
        output += [f'<!-- terminal: {", ".join(terminal)} -->', '']
    for start in range(0, len(events), EVENTS_PER_TABLE):
        cols = events[start:start + EVENTS_PER_TABLE]
        output += ['| State | ' + ' | '.join(cols) + ' |', '|---|' + '---|' * len(cols)]
        for state in states:
            output.append(f'| **{state}** | ' + ' | '.join(grid[state, event] for event in cols) + ' |')
        output.append('')
    notes = data.get('guard_notes', [])
    if not isinstance(notes, list) or not all(
            isinstance(note, str) and note.strip() and '\n' not in note for note in notes):
        raise ValueError('guard_notes must be a list of nonempty single lines')
    if notes:
        output += ['## Guard notes', '', *[f'- {note}' for note in notes], '']
    return '\n'.join(output)


def render_cell(cell: dict, states: list[str], repo: Path, sources: dict[str, list[str]]) -> str:
    disposition, target = cell.get('disposition'), cell.get('target')
    if not isinstance(disposition, str) or disposition not in DISPOSITIONS:
        raise ValueError('invalid disposition')
    if (disposition == 'transition' and target not in states) or (disposition != 'transition' and target is not None):
        raise ValueError('only a transition has a declared target')
    crash = cell.get('crash', False)
    question, decision = cell.get('q'), cell.get('dr')
    if type(crash) is not bool or (crash and disposition != 'handle'):
        raise ValueError('crash must be a boolean and requires handle')
    if question is not None and (not isinstance(question, str) or not re.fullmatch(r'Q-\d+', question)):
        raise ValueError('question must be Q-nn')
    if (disposition in HOLES or crash) and not question:
        raise ValueError('hole or crash needs a question')
    if decision is not None and (not isinstance(decision, str) or not re.fullmatch(r'DR-\d+', decision)):
        raise ValueError('decision must be DR-nnn')
    note = cell.get('note', '')
    if not isinstance(note, str) or any(marker in note for marker in ('\n', '\r', '|')):
        raise ValueError('note must be a single line without a table bar')
    if crash and not note.strip():
        raise ValueError('crash needs a note')
    citation = cell.get('citation')
    excerpt = ''
    src_index = {}
    if citation is not None:
        if not isinstance(citation, dict) or not isinstance(citation.get('file'), str):
            raise ValueError('citation needs a repository-relative file')
        name, line, fragment = citation['file'], citation.get('line'), citation.get('fragment')
        path = (repo / name).resolve()
        if not re.fullmatch(r'[\w./-]+\.[A-Za-z]{1,4}', name) or Path(name).is_absolute() or not path.is_relative_to(repo):
            raise ValueError('citation needs a repository-relative file')

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class GroupResult:
    name: str
    outcome: str                      # "proven" | "violation"
    findings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def _z3():
    try:
        import z3
        return z3
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise SystemExit(
            "guard_proofs needs z3-solver — install the dev dependencies: "
            "pip install -r tools/requirements-dev.txt "
            "(or: uv run --with-requirements tools/requirements-dev.txt ...)"
        ) from exc


def _witness(model, decls_of_interest) -> str:
    parts = []
    for d in model.decls():
        if not decls_of_interest or d.name() in decls_of_interest:
            parts.append(f"{d.name()}={model[d]}")
    return ", ".join(sorted(parts)) or "<any assignment>"


def check_group(name: str, guards, assumptions=(), has_else: bool = False) -> GroupResult:
    """Prove PA-1 (pairwise disjointness) and PA-2 (coverage) for one
    guard group under the declared NAT assumptions.

    guards: list of (label, z3.BoolRef) pairs.
    assumptions: iterable of z3.BoolRef (the NAT domain).
    has_else: True when the code has an explicit else branch — coverage
    is then discharged by construction and only disjointness is proven.
    """

    findings: list[str] = []

    for i in range(len(guards)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(guards)):
            (la, ga), (lb, gb) = guards[i], guards[j]
            s = z3.Solver()
            s.add(*assumptions)
            s.add(ga, gb)
            if s.check() == z3.sat:
                findings.append(
                    f"PA-1 overlap: {la!r} and {lb!r} both fire "
                    f"(witness: {_witness(s.model(), None)}) — order decides")

    # PA-2: the disjunction covers the domain, or an explicit else exists
    if not has_else:
        s = z3.Solver()
        s.add(*assumptions)
        s.add(z3.Not(z3.Or(*[g for _, g in guards])))

                f"PA-2 gap: no guard fires "
                f"(witness: {_witness(s.model(), None)}) — hole, or add an "
                f"explicit else and pass has_else=True with a citation")

    return GroupResult(name=name,
                       outcome="violation" if findings else "proven",
                       findings=findings)


def boundary_probe(guards, assignments) -> list[tuple[dict, list[str]]]:
    """Evaluate which guard labels fire for concrete assignments —
    below, exactly at, and above every comparison limit (02-pilot
    step 4c). assignments: list of {z3-const: python value} dicts.
    Returns [(assignment, [labels that fire]), ...] for the report.
    """
    z3 = _z3()

    def lift(v):
        if isinstance(v, bool):
            return z3.BoolVal(v)
        if isinstance(v, int):
            return z3.IntVal(v)
        if isinstance(v, float):
            return z3.RealVal(v)
        return v  # already a z3 expr

    rows = []
    for a in assignments:
        subs = [(var, lift(val)) for var, val in a.items()]
        labels = [label for label, g in guards
                  if z3.is_true(z3.simplify(z3.substitute(g, *subs)))]
        rows.append(({str(k): v for k, v in a.items()}, labels))
    return rows


def render(results) -> str:
    """guard-results.txt format: one outcome line per group, findings
    indented. not-formalizable groups are appended by the per-run
    script itself (they never reach z3)."""
    lines = []
    for r in results:
        lines.append(f"group {r.name}: {r.outcome}")
        lines.extend(f"  - {f}" for f in r.findings)
    return "\n".join(lines)

{"text": "=== INPUT 2: REQUIREMENTS (domain-analysis/circuitBreaker/requirements-prose.md) ===

The struct `CircuitBreaker` is a state machine to prevent sending requests that are likely to fail.
The function `NewCircuitBreaker` creates a new `CircuitBreaker`.


You can configure `CircuitBreaker` by the struct `Settings`:


- `Name` is the name of the `CircuitBreaker`.

- `MaxRequests` is the maximum number of requests allowed to pass through
  when the `CircuitBreaker` is half-open.
  If `MaxRequests` is 0, `CircuitBreaker` allows only 1 request.

- `Interval` is the cyclic period of the closed state
  for `CircuitBreaker` to clear the internal `Counts`, described later in this section.
  If `Interval` is 0, `CircuitBreaker` doesn't clear the internal `Counts` during the closed state.

- `Timeout` is the period of the open state,
  after which the state of `CircuitBreaker` becomes half-open.
  If `Timeout` is 0, the timeout value of `CircuitBreaker` is set to 60 seconds.

- `ReadyToTrip` is called with a copy of `Counts` whenever a request fails in the closed state.
  If `ReadyToTrip` returns true, `CircuitBreaker` will be placed into the open state.
  If `ReadyToTrip` is `nil`, default `ReadyToTrip` is used.
  Default `ReadyToTrip` returns true when the number of consecutive failures is more than 5.

- `OnStateChange` is called whenever the state of `CircuitBreaker` changes.

- `IsSuccessful` is called with the error returned from a request.
  If `IsSuccessful` returns true, the error is counted as a success.
  Otherwise the error is counted as a failure.
  If `IsSuccessful` is nil, default `IsSuccessful` is used, which returns false for all non-nil errors.

The struct `Counts` holds the numbers of requests and their successes/failures:


`CircuitBreaker` clears the internal `Counts` either
on the change of the state or at the closed-state intervals.
`Counts` ignores the results of the requests sent before clearing.

`CircuitBreaker` can wrap any function to send a request:


The method `Execute` runs the given request if `CircuitBreaker` accepts it.
`Execute` returns an error instantly if `CircuitBreaker` rejects the request.
Otherwise, `Execute` returns the result of the request.
If a panic occurs in the request, `CircuitBreaker` handles it as an error
and causes the same panic again.

from pathlib import Path
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / 'pack/tools'))
from guard_proofs import boundary_probe, check_group, render
from z3 import And, Bool, Int, Not

mode, requests, limit, successes, failures, before, current, duration = [
    Int(name) for name in ('mode', 'requests', 'limit', 'successes', 'failures', 'before', 'current', 'duration')]
u32 = 2**32 - 1
u64 = 2**64 - 1
groups = []

def group(name, guards, assumptions, probes):
    result = check_group(name, guards, assumptions)
    result.findings.append('Assumptions: ' + ', '.join(map(str, assumptions)))
    for assignment, branches in boundary_probe(guards, probes):
        result.findings.append(f'{assignment}: {", ".join(branches)}')
    groups.append(result)

modes = [mode >= 0, mode <= 2]
budget = [limit >= 1, limit <= u32, requests >= 0, requests <= u32]
open_guard = mode == 2
full_guard = And(mode == 1, requests >= limit)
group('G-01 admission', [('open', open_guard), ('full', full_guard),
      ('admit', And(Not(open_guard), Not(full_guard)))], modes + budget,
      [{mode:m, requests:r, limit:2} for m in range(3) for r in (1,2,3)])
group('G-02 generation', [('apply', before == current), ('discard', before != current)],
      [before >= 0, before <= u64, current >= 0, current <= u64],
      [{before:b,current:2} for b in (1,2,3)])
group('G-03 successful half-open completion', [('stay', successes < limit), ('close', successes >= limit)],
      [successes >= 0, successes <= u32, limit >= 1, limit <= u32],
      [{successes:s,limit:2} for s in (1,2,3)] + [{successes:0,limit:1},{successes:u32,limit:u32}])
group('G-04 default trip', [('stay', failures <= 5), ('trip', failures > 5)],
      [failures >= 0, failures <= u32], [{failures:f} for f in (4,5,6)])
group('G-07 duration defaults', [('default', duration <= 0), ('custom', duration > 0)],
      [duration >= -(2**63), duration < 2**63], [{duration:d} for d in (-1,0,1)])
group('G-07 request budget default', [('default', limit == 0), ('custom', limit != 0)],
      [limit >= 0, limit <= u32], [{limit:0},{limit:1}])
for ident, name in [('G-08','successful'), ('G-09','callbackPresent'), ('G-11','constructorPolicyPresent'),
                    ('G-11','errorNil'), ('G-12','intervalZero')]:
    flag = Bool(name)
    group(ident + ' ' + name, [('yes',flag), ('no',Not(flag))], [], [{flag:False},{flag:True}])
group('G-09 same-state suppression', [('no transition', mode == current), ('transition', mode != current)],
      modes + [current >= 0,current <= 2],
      [{mode:m,current:c} for m in range(3) for c in range(3)])
group('G-10 final available slot', [('stay', requests + 1 < limit), ('saturate', requests + 1 == limit)],
      budget + [requests < limit], [{requests:0,limit:2},{requests:1,limit:2}])
group('G-12 mode dispatch', [('closed',mode == 0), ('half-open',mode == 1), ('open',mode == 2)],
      modes, [{mode:m} for m in range(3)])

report = render(groups) + '\n'

report += 'group G-06 custom trip policy liveness: not-formalizable: external-call: user callback may panic or never return under the mutex.\n'
Path(__file__).with_name('guard-results.txt').write_text(report)
print(report,end='')
raise SystemExit(any(group.outcome != 'proven' for group in groups))

item.text: The bounded Go probes reproduced two callback reentry stalls, duplicate reports closing half-open early, and callback panics altering failure accounting or replacing the original panic. The blind pass returned coverage for every event and pair ordering. I’m now classifying its situations against the cited behavior.

|---|---|

| TestNewCircuitBreaker | Construction starts closed and establishes configured or default state data. observed-in-tests gobreaker_test.go:126 ("func TestNewCircuitBreaker(t *testing.T) {"). |

| TestCustomCircuitBreaker | Closed interval clears, custom failure ratio opens, timeout permits half-open, third pending admission saturates, fourth rejects, and third success closes. observed-in-tests gobreaker_test.go:259 ("assert.Error(t, succeed(customCB))"). Line 247 reads defaultCB expiry, so it supplies no custom expiry assertion. |
| TestTwoStepCircuitBreaker | Allow and report follow the same state path with no classifier. observed-in-tests gobreaker_test.go:307 ("assert.Nil(t, fail2Step(tscb))"). |
| TestPanicInRequest | Request panic is rethrown with one failure in the tested closed path. observed-in-tests gobreaker_test.go:325 ("assert.Panics(t, func() { causePanic(defaultCB) })"). |
| TestGeneration | State clears the interval before late completion, which does not alter refreshed counts. observed-in-tests gobreaker_test.go:342 ("assert.Equal(t, Counts{0, 0, 0, 0, 0}, customCB.counts)"). |

Controlled request scheduling uses channels. The half-open probes use a one-nanosecond timeout and a nanosecond-scale clock dependency. The reentry probe confirms no return in a 30 ms window after the callback entered. The mutex contract and held-lock call establish why reentry cannot complete. Blocked goroutines are local to the probe test process.

func Goexit()

README timing, classification, instant rejection and panic exceptions are traced to Q-01, Q-05, Q-15 and Q-10. OnStateChange means enum changes, including lazily observed changes. Half-open saturation is a condition within the same public state. The README gives the closed trip result and does not prescribe the half-open exit rule, Q-04.

## Lint review

- Waiting and stopping. Saturated half-open has no time-based recovery with an unreported admission. User work and injected policy can block indefinitely. F-07, step-5 lint, Q-06. F-11, step-3 lock-discipline annotation, Q-09.
- Retry bound. No ordinary request retry engine. Execute recovery can attempt failure accounting again when the original accounting panics. F-03, step-8 verification, Q-10.
- External failure. Notification has no returned error or compensation; policy panic can escape and change what the caller sees. F-03, seam-contract sweep, Q-12 and Q-10.
- Cancellation and lifecycle disagreement. A caller exiting or losing its callback leaves the charged generation budget. The old wrapper stays reachable through a retained callback. F-07, step-5 lint, Q-06 and Q-17.
- Startup and diagnostics. Constructed Closed and refusal sentinels are explicit. There is no terminal or shutdown operation. A zero receiver has a different initialization and failure path. F-18, step-3 checklist, Q-08.
- Overload. Closed admits freely and stores counters but no pending queue. Half-open exhaustion has ErrTooManyRequests and no timeout. F-07, step-5 lint, Q-06. Counter representation is finite, F-05, z3 invariant check, Q-11.
- Synchronized reset. Open expiry admits a fresh local budget; HalfOpen success removes the admission cap. F-10, multi-instance probes, Q-14.
- Dual cleanup and async cancellation isolation. No owned resource destructor or internal async queue. Execute recovery and two-step reports are distinct API forms; duplicate logical completion is reachable through repeated reports and through panic re-accounting. F-14, adversarial trace, Q-03. F-03, step-8 verification, Q-10.
- User-model gap. Admission at equality holds while another call is pending, and the observer can itself refresh state. A State read or earlier outcome can invalidate a later report. F-02, step-4 matrix walk, Q-04. F-05, step-5 lint, Q-02. F-15, adversarial trace, Q-05.

Scope is in [scope.md](scope.md). One constructed instance starts Closed (the zero enum), then explicitly initializes a generation. HalfOpen has no expiry and can have spare admission budget or full budget. Full budget can coexist with pending or abandoned work. Because reports can repeat, reported outcomes need not correspond one-to-one with admissions. Public State reports the same enum for both half-open conditions. observed-in-code gobreaker.go:285 ("cb.counts.Requests >= cb.maxRequests"). gobreaker.go:299 ("if generation != before {"). gobreaker.go:315 ("cb.counts.onSuccess()"). gobreaker.go:370 ("if cb.interval == 0 {"). gobreaker.go:376 ("cb.expiry = now.Add(cb.timeout)"). gobreaker.go:378 ("cb.expiry = zero").
- Constructor normalizes zero max to one, nonpositive interval to zero, nonpositive timeout to sixty seconds, and nil policies to defaults. Name and callbacks are fixed after publication for supported calls. Settings is passed by value and function values may capture mutable state. observed-in-code gobreaker.go:144 ("cb.name = st.Name"). gobreaker.go:148 ("cb.maxRequests = 1"). gobreaker.go:154 ("cb.interval = defaultInterval"). gobreaker.go:160 ("cb.timeout = defaultTimeout"). gobreaker.go:166 ("cb.readyToTrip = defaultReadyToTrip"). gobreaker.go:172 ("cb.isSuccessful = defaultIsSuccessful"). gobreaker.go:190 ("const defaultTimeout = time.Duration(60) * time.Second").

# CircuitBreaker domain behaviour pilot

model routing: on (unevaluated, cascade plan stage 3)
routing variant: matrix
Jev: jev-1.14.0. Baseline: 27b8e2cfc65aacd09abb3968455e4b01df4a83fa.

The primary deliverable is [open-questions.md](open-questions.md). The matrix projects a constructed instance and divides HalfOpen by admission budget. In-flight work, callback execution and mutex ownership are separate tracks described in the traces. Compound cells show one target and describe other branches in text. There are no terminal states or behavioural decisions in this run. No library, existing test, or configuration files were changed.

## Verified findings and coverage

| Applicable case | Evidence and consequence | Question |
|---|---|---|
| Expiry with no input, at equality, or overdue | UV-19, T-11 and T-20. State, admission and outcome can observe a strict deadline; Counts alone can expose stale counters. gobreaker.go:220, 337-342. | Q-01, Q-02 |
| Same caller repeats while Execute is pending | UV-03, T-02. Channel probe reproduces the second request finishing first. Same gate applies at the half-open boundary. gobreaker.go:242, 277-289. | Q-04, Q-07 |
| Same caller repeats while returned callback is outstanding | UV-03, T-03, P-06b. Distinct Allow calls consume distinct budget slots; one success does not refund or satisfy the other. gobreaker.go:266-273, 285-289. | Q-04, Q-07 |
| Duplicate and opposite outcomes | UV-11, UV-12, T-01 and T-14. The lock serializes reports; generation equality does not enforce once-only accounting. A repeated success can close with one distinct trial on a two-trial budget. gobreaker.go:271-272, 294-299, 315-318. | Q-03, Q-11 |
| Omitted, cancelled or delayed outcomes | UV-09, UV-10, UV-15, T-04 to T-06, T-10 and T-13. Without a later report, saturated half-open can stay full; a matching report can close or open it. Stale reports may reconcile time and notify before suppressing their accounting. The classifier can run regardless of accounting staleness. gobreaker.go:243, 271-272, 285-289, 298-306, 334-345. | Q-05, Q-06, Q-17, Q-19 |
| Callback completion and failure on both sides of commit | UV-16 to UV-18, T-06 to T-09. Trip policy reentry and notification reentry block on the same mutex. A policy panic can record two failures; a notification panic can replace an original request panic after transition commit. Classifier reentry is outside the lock and may advance generation. gobreaker.go:207, 234-243, 294-295, 325-327, 354-359. | Q-09, Q-10, Q-12, Q-15, Q-16 |
| Wrong receiver versus wrong hint or report | UV-07, UV-13, UV-14, T-12 and T-15. Valid wrong receivers operate independently; transferred reports target the captured wrapper. Nil and zero-value paths have different failure behavior. gobreaker.go:137, 228-243, 266-273. | Q-08, Q-13, Q-17 |
| Shared resource across instances | T-16 to T-18. Fixed local expiry can align half-open bursts. The capacity calculation comes from the modeled schedules. No service load test was performed. gobreaker.go:285, 342, 376. | Q-14 |
| Shutdown, destructor, queue inventory and retry | No public shutdown or implicit resource release path, no library queue or autonomous retry loop. Caller lifetime can end before accounting. The closure can keep the wrapper reachable. gobreaker.go:234-244, 262-274, 334-380. | Q-06, Q-17 |

The README rule for the default trip threshold and its stale-result sentence were both supported in Jev Choice but fell below the provisional scope cutoff. The two routed control verdicts were voided. Q-18 and Q-19 preserve the specific orderings. The pilot also records timing scope for exact expiry and instant rejection.

## Counts

4 states, 30 events including 19 undesired variants, 28 interaction pairs and 56 orderings, 120 cells, 23 UNSPECIFIED cells, 0 accidental ignores. 14 guard groups proven, 0 guard violations, 2 not formalizable. 17 consolidated behavior findings or contract gaps and 2 additional routing-scope questions give 19 open questions. The existing-test race is a separate validation finding. Part B returned 178 situations, with 86 convergent, 32 convergent-hole, 51 divergences folded into open questions, 1 catalogue artefact and 8 Part B blind spots.

## Executed checks and retained failures

- Baseline `go test -timeout=15s ./...` passed, log 011.
- Initial overlay passed seven probes, log 057. Expanded bounded overlay passed nine probes, log 108. The final nine probe cases also passed under `-race`, log 117.
- Full `go test -race -timeout=25s -count=1 -overlay domain-analysis/circuitBreaker/overlay.json ./...` failed, log 105. Existing TestCustomCircuitBreaker reads private counts at gobreaker_test.go:258 while another goroutine increments them. The production public Counts path takes the mutex. See as-is-validation.md.
- Catalogue render and matrix render succeeded, logs 118 and 119. The initial matrix wrapper run reported missing Q links before the question file existed, log 064. Re-run passed after the question file was written.
- Guard check completed with zero guard failures, log 129. The same run emitted the distinct-admission accounting counterexample `[limit = 2, successes = 2, requests = 1]`. See guard-results.txt.
- Blind coverage passed, log 125. The final catalogue includes a remembrance clarification from the diff. The dispatch package is preserved as sent.
- Source/test/configuration comparison to HEAD returned clean, log 127. The macOS git launcher emitted an xcrun cache warning in that command. The pilot read-only count command in log 132 initially assumed keyed cells; the corrected count in log 133 iterated the sidecar list. The checker invocation with an unsupported help argument in log 112 failed independently of its successful gate invocation.
- The benchmark inputs provide no neighbouring model. The optional separate reviewer pass was not run. This pilot exercised ordering and callback defects with bounded Go probes; some wall-time and shared-resource schedules remain source-derived.

## Routing ledger

Drafts and all seam, scope, verification and blind requests completed. No provider failure or skipped provider call. Two draft citations failed their exact-fragment check and were corrected from the original sources. Jev did not judge those two fragments in draft-verify. Inspection and disposition details are in extraction.md. Part B was dispatched once after its final package inspection.

Completed the CircuitBreaker pilot in [domain-analysis/circuitBreaker](/private/tmp/stateradar-mutation-cost-matrix/selective/pool/domain-analysis/circuitBreaker/summary.md). The analysis covers 4 states, 30 events, 56 interaction orderings, and 120 matrix cells. All [19 domain questions](/private/tmp/stateradar-mutation-cost-matrix/selective/pool/domain-analysis/circuitBreaker/open-questions.md) remain open.

- A single TwoStep callback can report success twice and close a half-open breaker before two distinct trials complete. An omitted report can leave the half-open admission budget exhausted indefinitely.
- Synchronous reentry from `ReadyToTrip` or `OnStateChange` into a locking breaker method stalls. A trip-policy panic can count one failure twice, and a notification panic can replace the original request panic after the state change commits.
- A stale completion can trigger expiry reconciliation and notification before its outcome is discarded.

The baseline Go suite and all nine isolated probes passed. The full race-detector run flagged an unlocked counter read in the existing `TestCustomCircuitBreaker`. The isolated probes passed under the race detector. Source, existing tests, and configuration were left intact.

The strict sidecar, matrix, guards, reachability, blind coverage, and final audit passed. The [blind diff](/private/tmp/stateradar-mutation-cost-matrix/selective/pool/domain-analysis/circuitBreaker/part-b-diff.md) classified all 178 returned situations. All routed model calls completed.
